records.title: React Aria: Autocomplete
records.summary: An autocomplete allows users to search or filter a list of suggestions.
records.evidence_excerpt: An autocomplete allows users to search or filter a list of suggestions.

normalized_content.description: An autocomplete allows users to search or filter a list of suggestions.

props.name: children
props.description: The children wrapped by the autocomplete. Consists of at least an input element and a collection element to filter.

props.name: defaultInputValue
props.description: The default value of the autocomplete input (uncontrolled).

props.name: disableAutoFocusFirst
props.description: Whether or not to focus the first item in the collection after a filter is performed. Note this is only applicable if virtual focus behavior is not turned off via `disableVirtualFocus`.

props.name: disableVirtualFocus
props.description: Whether the autocomplete should disable virtual focus, instead making the wrapped collection directly tabbable.

props.name: filter
props.type: ((textValue: string, inputValue: string, node: Node<T>) => boolean) | undefined
props.description: An optional filter function used to determine if a option should be included in the autocomplete list. Include this if the items you are providing to your wrapped collection aren't filtered by default.

props.name: inputValue
props.description: The value of the autocomplete input (controlled).

props.name: onInputChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the autocomplete input value changes.

props.name: slot
props.description: A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all props received from a parent.

props.description: Whether to exclude the element from the sequential tab order. If true, the element will not be focusable via the keyboard by tabbing. props.name: form
props.description: The `<form>` element to associate the button with. The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document. See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/button#form).

props.description: The URL that processes the information submitted by the button. Overrides the action attribute of the button's form owner.

props.name: formEncType
props.description: Indicates how to encode the form data that is submitted.

props.name: formMethod
props.description: Indicates the HTTP method used to submit the form.

props.name: formNoValidate
props.description: Indicates that the form is not to be validated when it is submitted.

props.name: formTarget
props.description: Overrides the target attribute of the button's form owner.

props.name: id
props.description: The element's unique identifier. See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/id).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description: Whether the button is in a pending state. This disables press and hover events while retaining focusability, and announces the pending state to screen readers.

props.name: name
props.description: Submitted as a pair with the button's value as part of the form data.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

props.name: onClick
props.description: **Not recommended – use `onPress` instead.** `onClick` is an alias for `onPress` provided for compatibility with other libraries. `onPress` provides additional event details for non-mouse interactions.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

props.name: onFocusChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

props.name: onHoverChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the hover state changes.

props.name: onHoverEnd
props.description: Handler that is called when a hover interaction ends.

props.name: onHoverStart
props.description: Handler that is called when a hover interaction starts.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.

props.name: onKeyUp
props.description: Handler that is called when a key is released.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Handler that is called when the press is released over the target.

props.name: onPressChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the press state changes.

props.name: onPressEnd
props.description: Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.

props.name: onPressStart
props.description: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.

props.name: onPressUp
props.description: Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of whether it started on the target or not.

props.name: preventFocusOnPress
props.description: Whether to prevent focus from moving to the button when pressing it. Caution, this can make the button inaccessible and should only be used when alternative keyboard interaction is provided, such as ComboBox's MenuTrigger or a NumberField's increment/decrement control.

props.description: The behavior of the button when used in an HTML form.

props.name: value
props.description: The value associated with the button's name when it's submitted with the form data.

props.name: altKey` \*
props.description: Whether the alt keyboard modifier was held during the press event.

props.name: ctrlKey` \*
props.description: Whether the ctrl keyboard modifier was held during the press event.

props.name: metaKey` \*
props.description: Whether the meta keyboard modifier was held during the press event.

props.name: pointerType` \*
props.description: The pointer type that triggered the press event.

props.name: shiftKey` \*
props.description: Whether the shift keyboard modifier was held during the press event.

props.name: target` \*
props.description: The target element of the press event.

props.name: type` \*
props.description: The type of press event being fired.

props.name: x` \*
props.description: X position relative to the target.

props.description: Y position relative to the target.

props.description: The key that triggered the press event, if it was triggered by a keyboard interaction. This is useful for differentiating between Space and Enter key presses.

accessibility_notes.text: A FocusScope manages focus for its descendants. It supports containing focus inside the scope, restoring focus to the previously focused element on unmount, and auto focusing children on mount. It also acts as a container for a programmatic focus management interface that can be used to move focus forward and back in response to user events.

`FocusScope` is a utility component that can be used to manage focus for its descendants. When the `contain` prop is set, focus is contained within the scope. This is useful when implementing overlays like modal dialogs, which should not allow focus to escape them while open. In addition, the `restoreFocus` prop can be used to restore focus back to the previously focused element when the focus scope unmounts, for example, back to a button which opened a dialog. A FocusScope can also optionally…

A basic example of a focus scope that contains focus within it is below. Clicking the "Open" button mounts a FocusScope, which auto focuses the first input inside it. Once open, you can press the <Keyboard>Tab</Keyboard> key to move within the scope, but focus is contained inside. Clicking the "Close" button unmounts the focus scope, which restores focus back to the button. For a full example of building a modal dialog, see [useDialog](Modal/useModalOverlay.md#usedialog).

This example shows how to use `useFocusManager` to programmatically move focus within a `FocusScope`. It implements a basic toolbar component, which allows using the left and right arrow keys to move focus to the previous and next buttons. The `wrap` option is used to make focus wrap around when it reaches the first or last button.

accessibility_notes.text: By default, GridList uses arrow key navigation to move focus into rows. Set `keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab"` to have <Keyboard>Tab</Keyboard> move focus in and out of a cell. Use this when cells contain interactive elements such as text fields, where arrow keys and typing in the field should not trigger grid navigation or selection.

accessibility_notes.text: Toast regions are [landmark regions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/landmark-regions/) that can be navigated using <Keyboard>F6</Keyboard> to move forward and <Keyboard>Shift</Keyboard> + <Keyboard>F6</Keyboard> to move backward. This provides an easy way for keyboard users to jump to toasts from anywhere in the app. When a toast is closed, focus moves to the next toast if any. When the last toast is closed, focus is restored to where it was before.
